public_body: Fitchburg Housing Authority Board Of Commissioners
overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on the locked-door access and pre-meeting Wallace Towers discussion allegations, and noted but did not penalize deficient draft minutes, which it urged the Board to amend.

allegations.summary: Complainant said the meeting room doors were locked and she gained entry only after members of the public let her in, though the meeting notice gave 1:00 p.m.
allegations.key_passage: Because it is clear that the Complainant was able to access the meeting prior to its start, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law with respect to the accessibility of its June 28 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged Wallace Towers Project updates were discussed with a quorum of Board members before the June 28 meeting was formally convened, a topic not on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: However, the complaint does not specifically allege that any member of the Board discussed the project and there has been no specific evidence presented to support a finding that the Board deliberated prior to the formal start of the June 28 meeting.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint, the AG reviewed the posted draft minutes of the June 28 meeting, which had no summary of discussion and listed motions without recorded votes.
allegations.key_passage: The draft minutes of the June 28 meeting posted online fall far short of the accuracy requirement where they include absolutely no summary of any discussion and where they list three motions made but do not record any votes taken.
